title: Beebe Vent Field: the deepest black smokers

briefing.summary: Descend to the Beebe Hydrothermal Vent Field on the Mid-Cayman Spreading Centre and scan its black-smoker chimneys and the Rimicaris shrimp swarms living around them. A western sulfide mound offers another nearby target.
facts: Beebe lies about 4,960 m deep in the discovery survey (Connelly et al. 2012); its nearby game targets sit on terrain around 4,957–4,988 m.
Its low-salinity vent fluid has been measured around 401–403 °C at roughly 500 bar, hot and pressurized enough to become supercritical.
Rimicaris hybisae swarm the chimneys; their enlarged dorsal eyes detect light without forming images, and may sense faint vent light and bioluminescence.
The field sits on the Mid-Cayman Spreading Centre, the world's deepest and one of its slowest-spreading mid-ocean ridges (~15 mm/yr).
hazards: Rated depth: this Class C hull can operate to 11,000 m, giving wide margin here, but treat the pressure at nearly 5,000 m as real and unforgiving.
Scalding, chemically hostile fluid at the chimney mouths -- some of it supercritical, hotter than 400 degC. Do not linger inside a plume.
No sunlight reaches this depth; use your lights to read the chimneys and surrounding seabed.
Von Damm, this ridge's other major vent field, lies about 21 km south-southwest at ~2,300 m -- well outside this survey's tile and not reachable in this mission.

objectives.title: Scan the Beebe 1–5 smokers
objectives.hint: Find the black-smoker complex on the Mid-Cayman seafloor, near 4,990 m.

objectives.title: Scan the Rimicaris hybisae swarm
objectives.hint: Look beside the Beebe chimneys for shrimp, around 4,980 m.

objectives.title: Survey the western sulfide mound
objectives.hint: Head southwest from the main chimneys to the mound, near 4,960 m.
